analysis.title: Postponed but not abandoned: the Fed holds key rates steady but keeps focus on elevated inflation
key_insights: The FOMC held its policy rate at 3.75%-4.00% at the October 2026 meeting, as expected. Two voting members dissented in favour of an immediate hike: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack.
Cook's hawkish dissent was surprising. She had been regarded as a dovish member and had not dissented before.

The statement was largely unchanged, but growth was upgraded to 'expanded at a strong pace' from September's 'expanded at a solid pace'. The statement also describes productivity growth as strong and capital investment as robust.

Chair Warsh said first-half GDP growth was revised up from 1.8% to 2.4% and that Q3 appeared even stronger. He said the FOMC believes the September rate increase is starting to restrain activity, though conditions are not yet tight.

Warsh said financial and credit conditions have tightened for some businesses and households, that investors are becoming more selective in allocating capital, and that AI is not divorced from interest rates.
Warsh again rejected forward guidance ('I don't believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis'). The next decision is hard to predict from Fed communication.
The Fed will move to eight meetings a year, with one meeting in 2027 and two in 2028 focused on strategy rather than rate decisions. The Fed's task forces are not close to conclusions.

Market reaction was muted: the dollar was slightly softer, the 2-year yield fell from its post-statement high, the 10-year yield rose first (steeper curve) and then declined, and the S&P 500 closed modestly higher.
Syz expects the next hike in December, in line with market pricing, and only one hike in 2027 (in the first half). Markets price about 1.5 hikes for 2027.
Warsh said the meeting 'focused mainly on the price stability side of our remit' and called the employment side 'quite positive', which Syz reads as inflation being the dominant concern.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates held, with two dissents in favour of a hike. The Fed raised rates in September.
Warsh cited the upward revision as evidence that the economy was stronger than previously thought.

macro_indicators.reading: Described by Warsh as appearing even stronger than the first half
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports the hawkish tone. No numeric figure is given in the text.
Syz agrees with market pricing for a December hike.

macro_indicators.reading: One hike, in the first half of 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Syz is below market pricing, which implies about 1.5 hikes. Syz sees no aggressive hiking cycle.
Markets price more tightening than Syz expects.

risk_factors: Inflation remains well above the Fed's 2% target and could force more hikes than Syz expects.
Tighter financial and credit conditions could slow activity more than expected.
Warsh rejects forward guidance, so the rate path is less predictable.
The Trump administration's attempt to remove Governor Cook adds institutional risk. Hearings are planned for next week.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price about 1.5 hikes in 2027, on persistently elevated inflation and strong growth with Warsh's focus on price stability.
tension_points.bear_case: Syz expects only one hike in the first half of 2027. Tighter financial conditions, wider spreads and higher yields should gradually cool activity, and consumption should be moderated by elevated price pressures.
